blocks.text: Simon Fraser University SFU home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

87 condos sold in Simon Fraser University SFU with a median price of $512,000 (the middle half sold between $437,500 and $606,500), taking a median of 39 days to sell at 96.8% of the last list price; 8% sold above list. They had a median $635 per square foot, a median year built of 2012 and a median strata fee of $491 a month. 7 townhomes sold in Simon Fraser University SFU with a median price of $825,000, taking a median of 34 days to sell at 96.9% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $582 per square foot, a median year built of 2014 and a median strata fee of $799 a month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Simon Fraser Univer.

Tenure flag, stated at the top — this area's defining fact: every market home in UniverCity is LEASEHOLD PREPAID strata on a 99-year ground lease from SFU Community Trust — the land remains under SFU ownership and the Trust leases fully serviced, subdivided parcels to developers through 99-year lease agreements, so UniverCity homes are leasehold, not freehold. A current listing states the structure in MLS terms as "Leasehold prepaid-Strata" and another states "Leasehold expires in 2109" for its building. This area has no page yet on jaredgibbons.ca.
Crescent Court by Liberty Homes — 8725 University Crescent (also 8761 University Crescent)

Two towers of 14 and 20 storeys over a 3-storey townhouse podium beside Richard Bolton Park: 185 apartments and 14 townhomes, completed 2022 per the developer-source pages and current listings, which record Apartment/Condo type. The 14 townhomes are part of this development and are not counted again below. Published rental/pet restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
The Nest by Mosaic — 9250 University High Street

A five-storey building of 80 condo units per the construction source; current listings record year built 2012, Apartment/Condo, Subdivision Name "The Nest," ownership "Leasehold prepaid-Strata," and one listing states "Pets & rental allow" with cats OK in its pet field.
Origin — 9150 University High Street

Current listings name the building "Origin," record Apartment/Condo type and cats OK in the pet field, and one listing states "Leasehold expires in 2109." Year built conflicts by source: one current listing records 2012 and another records 2013 — flagged, not resolved. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.
Altitude by Hungerford Properties — 9060 University Crescent (Altitude Tower 1) and 9080 University Crescent

A concrete condo development in the heart of UniverCity; a directory records Altitude Tower 1 at 9060 University Crescent as 112 units, 14 storeys, built 2014, while listings at 9080 University Crescent record year built 2015 and describe "Pets & rentals allowed" — the year difference is the two towers' records, flagged here rather than merged.
Centre Block by Liberty Homes — 9393 Tower Road

A current listing names the building "Centre Block" by Liberty Homes in the heart of UniverCity and records a Simon Fraser Univer. condo for sale at this address. Year built, unit count and published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
The Hub by Liberty Homes — 9009 Cornerstone Mews
A current listing names the building "The HUB" by Liberty Homes, records year built 2009, Apartment/Condo type and Simon Fraser Univer. sub-area. Unit count and published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Terraces at the Peak by Intergulf — 8940 University Crescent

Current listings name the building "Terraces at the Peak" by Intergulf, describe a concrete building in UniverCity and record Simon Fraser Univer. condos for sale at this address. Year built, unit count and published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.

items.t: The area is the top of Burnaby Mountain in the City of Burnaby, comprising the Simon Fraser University (SFU) Burnaby campus and the UniverCity residential community beside it; the board sub-area is listed as "Simon Fraser Univer." and SnapStats prints the full name as "Simon Fraser University SFU." A separate neighbouring sub-area, "Simon Fraser Hills," covers the Forest Grove side and is not this area.

Where the condo stock concentrates: in UniverCity's four neighbourhoods — West Highlands, East Highlands, High Street and the Slopes — around University High Street, University Crescent and Tower Road, south and east of campus; the OCP envisions a dense, mixed-use community on about 65 hectares allowing up to 4,536 residential units housing up to 10,000 residents at build-out.

Transit: TransLink's R5 Hastings St RapidBus terminates at the SFU Exchange, running at least every 10 minutes at peak and 15 minutes off-peak to Burrard Station; the 145 bus connects SFU Exchange to Production Way–University Station on the Millennium Line. The proposed Burnaby Mountain Gondola is not yet approved or funded per TransLink.

Landmarks: the Burnaby Mountain Conservation Area surrounds the campus and community — 578 hectares, 34 multi-use trails over 28 kilometres, summit 366 metres — and shopping is centred on University High Street in the Cornerstone/High Street core.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Simon Fraser Univer.

items.t: Burnaby zoning — the current bylaw is new: the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (Bylaw No. 14815) was adopted June 9, 2026 and took effect July 1, 2026, replacing the former Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 1965 (No. 4742) — the 1965 bylaw is repealed and must not be cited as current if a source cites it. UniverCity itself was approved through OCP and zoning amendments in 1996 for the community south and east of campus.
Burnaby OCP: the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan was adopted December 9, 2025, replacing the 1998 OCP Bylaw; UniverCity is governed by its own OCP framework dating to the 1996 approvals.

Burnaby property tax: 2026 taxes were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes (and to an unclaimed home owner grant) after the July due date, with a further 5% penalty after the September due date.

blocks.text: Good to know about Simon Fraser Univer.

items.t: SFU gave up land to create the park that surrounds you. As part of the original arrangement, SFU transferred more than 320 hectares of university land to the City of Burnaby for the Burnaby Mountain Conservation Area — the community's setting is a negotiated conservation boundary, not an accident.

There are no fee-simple lots inside UniverCity at all. Every market home is a strata unit on the 99-year prepaid ground lease, so "lot size" comparisons between buildings come down to unit size, floor and outlook rather than land.

Two buildings share the "Cornerstone" name in different tenures. The Hub strata building sits on Cornerstone Mews (counted above), while the Cornerstone building at 8950 University High Street is presented in current sources as furnished student rentals — a search on the name alone mixes strata and rental product.

The elementary school inside the community is not the catchment for every mountain address. The SD41 locator returned Cameron Elementary for 8800 Eastlake Drive even though University Highlands Elementary sits inside UniverCity — location is not catchment on the mountain either.

Altitude's two towers carry two different built years in public records. The directory records Tower 1 (9060 University Crescent) as built 2014; listings at 9080 University Crescent record 2015 — a small example of why the strata plan registration, not a listing, settles a building's age.

Burnaby rewrote its entire zoning bylaw in 2026. The Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) took effect July 1, 2026 and replaced the 1965 bylaw (No. 4742) outright — any older source citing the 1965 bylaw for UniverCity is citing a repealed bylaw.

items.t: Simon Fraser Univer. is the top of Burnaby Mountain in the City of Burnaby: the Simon Fraser University (SFU) Burnaby campus and the UniverCity residential community beside it. The board sub-area is listed as "Simon Fraser Univer."; SnapStats prints the full name as "Simon Fraser University SFU." A separate neighbouring sub-area, "Simon Fraser Hills," covers the Forest Grove side of the mountain and is not this area. Nearby areas: Westridge, Lochdale, Sperling-Duthie (via Gaglardi Way), Forest Grove / Simon Fraser Hills, and Port Moody and Coquitlam across the mountain's east side.

UniverCity is a planned community on about 65 hectares, approved by the City of Burnaby in 1996 (OCP and zoning amendments), allowing up to 4,536 residential units in two neighbourhoods south and east of campus, housing up to 10,000 residents at build-out, built out in four neighbourhoods — West Highlands, East Highlands, High Street and the Slopes. The land remains under SFU ownership: SFU Community Trust leases fully serviced, subdivided parcels to developers through 99-year lease agreements, so UniverCity homes are leasehold, not freehold.
There are no conventional fee-simple residential lots inside UniverCity itself.
SnapStats publishes no SFU sub-area median.

Plan and zoning frame: the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan (adopted December 9, 2025, replacing the 1998 OCP Bylaw) is the citywide frame; UniverCity itself is governed by its own OCP framework dating to the 1996 approvals. City zoning is the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815, adopted June 9, 2026, in effect July 1, 2026) — never the former 1965 Bylaw No. 4742.

Schools (SD41; Ministry-listed names only): University Highlands Elementary is the elementary school inside UniverCity (LEED Gold certified; the school notes most families can walk to it in under 5 minutes); Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8800 Eastlake Drive) is the public secondary school on the mountain. The one locator run documented in the research is for 8800 Eastlake Drive: Cameron Elementary (K–7) / Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8–12) (SD41 School Locator, run 2026-11-01) — note the locator returns Cameron Elementary for the secondary school's own address even though University Highlands Elementary sits inside UniverCity; listing copy for Slopes Mews units states University Highlands Elementary / Burnaby Mountain Secondary catchments, which is listing copy, not a locator run. Catchments for other addresses: UNVERIFIED.

Setting: the Burnaby Mountain Conservation Area surrounding the campus and community covers 578 hectares with 34 multi-use trails over 28 kilometres, climbing from about 25 metres to the 366-metre summit; SFU transferred more than 320 hectares to the City for the conservation area as part of the original arrangement. Shopping is centred on University High Street in the Cornerstone/High Street core.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Simon Fraser Univer.

items.t: The ground lease is the governing document (this area's first rule): SFU Community Trust leases parcels to developers on 99-year leases and the land remains SFU's. Before anything else, confirm the lease commencement date, remaining term, whether rent is prepaid for the full term, and any rent-review or end-of-term provisions — the lease, not the building, is what a buyer's lender and lawyer will scrutinize.

Form B diligence (leasehold strata): a UniverCity strata is still a strata corporation under the Strata Property Act, so s. 59 applies — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. The Form B does not answer the ground-lease questions above — read both packages.

City property taxes (2026): City of Burnaby property taxes for 2026 were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes (and to an unclaimed home owner grant) after the July due date, with a further 5% penalty after the September due date.

blocks.text: Good to know about Simon Fraser Univer.

items.t: The university gave the city a mountain.

The elementary school beside you may not be your catchment school. The SD41 locator returns Cameron Elementary for 8800 Eastlake Drive — Burnaby Mountain Secondary's own address — even though University Highlands Elementary sits inside UniverCity a short walk away. Listing copy that states catchments (Slopes Mews listings name University Highlands) is copy, not a locator run.

The lease expiry is printed in listings, if you look. A current Origin listing states "Leasehold expires in 2109" in its body copy — the ground-lease term is a searchable, comparable fact between buildings, and the oldest (early-2000s) and newest buildings do not carry the same remaining term.
One development, two spellings, one count.

The community was planned whole. UniverCity's OCP allows up to 4,536 units housing up to 10,000 residents on about 65 hectares in neighbourhoods south and east of campus — the "still building out" feel (Arbour in the Slopes is the current phase) is the plan working as approved in 1996, not sprawl.
Winter is a pricing fact nobody publishes.
The 7% sales ratio is the negotiation.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Simon Fraser University Area?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 91 condos and townhomes listed in Simon Fraser University Area. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Simon Fraser University Area a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Simon Fraser University Area had a sales ratio of 7%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Simon Fraser University Area from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 30 condos and townhomes sold in Simon Fraser University Area over those 4 months, out of 750 in all of Burnaby.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did condos in Simon Fraser University SFU sell for?
faq.a: 87 condos sold in Simon Fraser University SFU between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $512,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Simon Fraser University SFU?
faq.a: The median was 39 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 96.8% of the last list price (8% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Are UniverCity homes freehold or leasehold?
faq.a: Leasehold prepaid. The land remains under SFU ownership; SFU Community Trust leases serviced parcels to developers through 99-year lease agreements, and buyers hold a leasehold strata interest — a current Origin listing states its lease expires in 2109. Never price or finance a unit here as freehold.

faq.q: Can I rent out a UniverCity condo long-term?
faq.a: Strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, and current listings at The Nest and Altitude state pets and rentals are allowed — but occupancy demand is heavily student-driven and the ground lease and strata documents still govern everything else, so verify building by building.

faq.q: Which schools serve a UniverCity address?
faq.a: University Highlands Elementary (SD41) sits inside the community and was designed so most families can walk to it in under 5 minutes; Burnaby Mountain Secondary is the public secondary school on the mountain.

Not as an approved project: TransLink states the Burnaby Mountain Gondola is not yet approved or funded and still needs a future investment plan plus TransLink Board and Mayors' Council approval. Treat it as upside, not current transit.

faq.q: Does the remaining lease term affect price between old and new buildings?
faq.a: Check each building's lease commencement on title instead of assuming.

No — nothing in UniverCity is freehold. SFU Community Trust leases serviced parcels to developers through 99-year prepaid ground leases; you buy a leasehold interest in a strata unit (a current Origin listing states "Leasehold expires in 2109").

faq.q: So where are the townhouses on the mountain?
faq.a: Inside the developments: Crescent Court (14 townhomes beside 185 apartments), Terraces at the Peak (townhouse units at 8980 University Crescent), Slopes Mews buildings (townhouse-form units at 9168/9228 Slopes Mews, 9888 University Crescent), and the Arbour presale's stacked townhomes (9688 University Crescent).

faq.q: What should I read first on a UniverCity purchase — the Form B or the ground lease?
faq.a: Both, in that order of risk: the Form B for the strata's finances and bylaws, and the ground lease for commencement date, remaining term, prepaid status and end-of-term provisions. The lease is what a lender and lawyer will scrutinize; some lenders cap mortgage terms against the remaining lease term (general guidance — UNVERIFIED per lender).
